content: 1. The instructions for the preparation and use of cefepime should be provided to the individuals responsible for performing the reconstitution steps. 2. To open the packaging, peel back the overwrap at the corner and remove the solution container. 3. Some cloudiness or opacity of the plastic may be observed due to moisture absorption during the sterilization process. This is a normal occurrence and does not compromise the quality or safety of the solution. The opacity will gradually diminish over time. 4. Remove the protective covers from both the top of the vial and the vial port on the diluent container as follows: To remove the breakaway vial cap, swing the pull ring over the top of the vial and pull downward to initiate the opening. Then, pull straight up to fully remove the cap. Do not access the vial with a syringe after the breakaway cap has been removed. To remove the vial port cover, grasp the tab on the pull ring, pull upward to break the three tie strings, and then pull back to remove the cover. 5. Screw the vial into the vial port until it cannot be turned further. Ensure the vial is tightly screwed in to create a proper seal. This typically requires approximately a half-turn (180°) after the first audible click. Note that the clicking sound alone does not guarantee a seal; the vial must be turned as far as it will go. Once the vial is seated, do not attempt to remove it. 6. Recheck the vial to confirm it is tightly secured by attempting to turn it further in the direction of assembly. Label the container appropriately. 7. To reconstitute the drug: Gently squeeze the bottom of the diluent container to inflate the portion surrounding the end of the drug vial. Using the other hand, push the drug vial downward into the container, telescoping the walls of the container. Grasp the inner cap of the vial through the container walls. Pull the inner cap from the drug vial. Verify that the rubber stopper has been removed, allowing the drug and diluent to mix. Mix the contents of the container thoroughly and use the solution within the specified time frame. Inspect the bottom of the vial to confirm that the stopper has been removed and complete mixing has occurred. If the rubber stopper is not removed and the medication is not released on the first attempt, the inner cap may be manipulated back into the rubber stopper without removing the drug vial from the diluent container. 8. Confirm the activation and admixture of the vial contents. Check for leaks by firmly squeezing the container. If leaks are detected, discard the unit as sterility may be compromised. 9. Close the flow control clamp on the administration set. Remove the cover from the outlet port at the bottom of the container. Insert the piercing pin of the administration set into the port with a twisting motion until the pin is firmly seated. Refer to the full directions provided on the administration set carton. 10. Lift the free end of the hanger loop on the bottom of the vial, breaking the two tie strings. Bend the loop outward to lock it in the upright position, then suspend the container from the hanger. 11. Squeeze and release the drip chamber to establish the proper fluid level within the chamber. Open the flow control clamp to clear air from the set, then close the clamp. 12. Attach the administration set to the venipuncture device. If the device is not indwelling, prime the set and perform venipuncture. Regulate the rate of administration using the flow control clamp. 13. Warning: Do not use flexible containers in series connections.
